text: At last she spoke to me. <break time="0.8s" /> And when she addressed the first words to me. <break time="0.8s" /> I was so confused. <break time="0.8s" /> That I did not know what to answer. <break time="0.8s" /> She asked me. <break time="0.8s" /> Whether I was going to Araby. <break time="0.8s" /> And she said. <break time="0.8s" /> That it would be a splendid bazaar. <break time="0.8s" /> And that she would love to go. <break time="0.8s" /> She could not go, however. <break time="0.8s" /> Because there would be a retreat. <break time="0.8s" /> That week in her convent school. <break time="0.8s" /> While she spoke. <break time="0.8s" /> She turned a silver bracelet. <break time="0.8s" /> Round and round her wrist. <break time="0.8s" /> And the light from the lamp. <break time="0.8s" /> Caught the white curve of her neck. <break time="0.8s" /> It is well for you, she said. <break time="0.8s" /> And I answered. <break time="0.8s" /> If I go. <break time="0.8s" /> I will bring you something. <break time="0.8s" /> What innumerable follies. <break time="0.8s" /> Laid waste. <break time="0.8s" /> My waking and sleeping thoughts. <break time="0.8s" /> After that evening. <break time="0.8s" /> I wished to annihilate. <break time="0.8s" /> The tedious days in between and the serious work of life. <break time="0.8s" /> Seemed to me. <break time="0.8s" /> Ugly, monotonous childs play. <break time="0.8s" /> At school I could not concentrate. <break time="0.8s" /> And the syllables of the word Araby. <break time="0.8s" /> Were called to me. <break time="0.8s" /> Through the silence. <break time="0.8s" /> Casting an Eastern enchantment over me.
